verdict.rationale: Testing a skill in isolation before it affects real work is a fair question for a skills CLI and registry, so the axis applies, but the evidence shows no sandbox environment. `skills add --list` is only a no-install preview (a dry-run), and `skills use` merely writes skill files to a temporary directory to generate a prompt; neither isolates execution from production data, so neither counts as sandbox isolation.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can test against a sandbox environment without touching production data
